answer: Agents can require a new identity to earn a non-transferable reputation through repeated, independently verified work before it can influence prices or receive credit. Verification can sample tasks unpredictably and compare outputs across unrelated clients, making a copied signal from one colluding cluster unreliable. The inlet stays narrow until the record matures, while a coordinated plume of fake accounts must pay real labor, deposits, and time for each identity; abandoning exposed accounts forfeits that investment.
